title: The Notch ligand Jagged1 regulates extracellular matrix production and organization in breast cancer
projectDescription: Data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry was used to study the effect of JAG1 protein in ECM organization in breast cancer. TNBC cell line samples including MDA-MB-231 cells (Jag1WT), JAG1 knock-out of MDA-MB-231 cells (Jag1KO), empty vector transfected to Jag1KO, and JAG1 rescued to Jag1KO cocultured with mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) as spheroids were used to compare the ECM proteins by mass spectrometry.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Spheroids of Jag1WT, Jag1KO, Jag1KO+empty vector, Jag1KO+JAG1 rescue vector, each co-cultured with mouse fibroblast (MEF) cells (4 replicates per coculture spheroid) were decellularized and the protein extracts were reduced and alkylated. The proteins were then digested with Trypsin/Lys-C in S-Trap microcolumn. The digested peptides were desalted and then injected into Q Exactive HF Orbitrap mass spectrometer. The peptides were separated with mobile phase buffer A (0.1% formic acid) and B (acetonitrile/water (95:5(v/v)), over a 50-minute gradient (8–35% B in 40 min, 35-100% B in 2 min and held at 100% B for 8 min). Data acquisition was performed with DIA mode, in which each cycle of full scan of 366-1007 m/z at a resolution of 120,000 was performed. DIA MS2 scans at a resolution of 30,000 were performed for all DIA scans with 40 fixed windows (17 m/z) overlapped by 1 m/z.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry raw data were processed by Spectronaut software (version 16.3) using directDIA workflow with a FASTA database containing human reviewed sequences along with their isoforms of UniprotKB release of 2022_01. Carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed modification and oxidation (K, M, P residues) and N-terminal protein acetylation were set as variable modifications. A maximum of five variable modifications per peptide was allowed and the false discovery rate was set at 1%. Precursors were filtered with q value and quantitation was done at MS2 level based on peak areas. Statistical analyses were done with Perseus (version 1.6.14.0) based on MS2 quantification data. Welch's T-test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR of 0.05 was used to identify statistically significant proteins from the comparisons.
